gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: Cut the onions, fry them gently and ___, stir in the cream.
gaps.hint: the last step of a sequence
gaps.explanation: 'Finally' closes a list of actions; 'firstly' opens one, while 'initially'/'at first' contrast with later events.

gaps.sentence: I'll tell you everything ___ you promise to keep it between us.
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' sets the condition attached to the promise.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: ___ you book soon, there won't be any seats left.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if... not': if you don't book soon, no seats.

gaps.sentence: The scheme is costly; on the ___ hand, it would create hundreds of jobs.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' balances a drawback against an advantage.

gaps.sentence: After years of setbacks, the tunnel was ___ completed in 2019.
gaps.explanation: 'Eventually' = in the end, after a long delay or difficulty.

gaps.sentence: The drug trial was halted ___ an irregularity in the data.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to' + noun phrase gives the reason in formal register.
